title: A stronger liquid surface
hook: Change surface tension and predict capillary-rise height.
misconception: capillary-rise height stays fixed when surface tension doubles.
objective: Apply h = 2γ cosθ/(ρgr) to compare capillary-rise height when surface tension changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With fixed tube radius density gravity and contact angle, h = 2γ cosθ/(ρgr). When surface tension doubles, capillary-rise height becomes 2 times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model h = 2γ cosθ/(ρgr); scaling exponent 1. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider fixed tube radius density gravity and contact angle, with a nonzero initial result. If surface tension triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on capillary-rise height?
recall.why: Apply h = 2γ cosθ/(ρgr) under the same assumptions: the multiplier is 3.
